title: Communication, speech, and language development in children (with neuromuscular disease): The first two years of life
summary:
Speech sound disorders and developmental language disorders are among the most common developmental disorders in childhood. Early detection of speech and language disorders in German-speaking countries is currently available for children at two years of age, although, according to international research, signs of developmental disorders can be observed as early as the first two years of life. In addition to their value for the early detection of speech and language disorders, deviations in the course of communication, speech, and language development within the first two years of life have been found to be clinical markers for profound developmental disorders. Because neuromuscular diseases (NMDs) are rare, very little is known about the communication, speech, and language development of children with NMD.
The aim of this project is to investigate for the first time in German-speaking countries the possibility of systematic and reliable monitoring of early communication, speech, and language development in children—specifically children with NMD—via online parental questionnaires at the age points of 3–5, 6–8, 9–12, 13–18, and/or 19–24 months. This could improve the prevention of communication, speech, and language disorders prior to two years of age. Additionally, it may allow for parental guidance, advice, and the initiation of early intervention, if necessary.
Participants in this study are families with children aged 0–2 years. Arm 1 includes 350-500 children without a (suspected) diagnosis of a developmental disorder (300-450 cross-sectional, 50 longitudinal), and Arm 2 includes 60 children with a (suspected) diagnosis of NMD. Caregivers are asked to complete age-specific online parental questionnaires either once (cross-sectional) or repeatedly (longitudinal), and to submit short audio or video files.
For some children (Arm 1: children participating longitudinally, Arm 2: if not provided by the serving medical institution), a test on general development (Bayley-III) will be offered.  Additionally, children with NMD (Arm 2) aged 2;0-2;11 having participated in the questionnaires will be offered a SLP assessment with standardized tests (SETK-II; PLAKSS-II).
